comparison: Perfect agreement on STITCH design and validation (C1, C2, C7, C93, C94, C96). Both evaluations find the basic characterization and functionality well-supported without concerns.

Strong agreement on position-dependent enhancer blocking effects (C3-C6). Both evaluations accept the ~20-fold effect on gene expression and correlation between MYC transcription and contact frequencies. OpenEval additionally includes C8 (4C-seq validation) which peer reviewers questioned separately.

Divergence on C8: OpenEval finds 4C-seq data supporting enhancer blocking, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting Hi-C/5C data and noting that structural changes don't correlate with endogenous CTCF sites.

Major disagreement on RNA-seq analysis (C9-C11, C54-C55, C60-C61). OpenEval finds comprehensive support with appropriate statistics, while peer reviewers raise significant concerns about loose cutoffs (p=0.1), single clone analysis, and paradoxical finding that STITCH has more deregulated genes than deletion.
Agreement on PVT1 findings (C12, C56). Both evaluations accept that PVT1 expression remains unchanged while MYC is affected, supporting minimal trans-acting lncRNA role.

Substantial agreement on mutational analysis (C13, C63-C68). Both accept graded effects and dose-dependent relationships. Peer reviewers note confusion about mechanisms (loop extrusion vs enhancer blocking) but don't challenge the data itself.

Strong agreement on power law scaling (C14-C15). Both evaluations find the non-linear relationship between contact frequency and expression well-supported and an important contribution, though peer reviewers request clarification of explanation.

Major disagreement on PCA analysis (C17, C70-C72). OpenEval finds sophisticated analysis showing preferential associations, while peer reviewers find it 'extremely confusing and convoluted' and request removal or radical simplification.

Significant disagreement on ChIP-seq quality (C18-C21, C73-C77). OpenEval finds comprehensive, localized epigenetic changes with proper controls, while peer reviewers raise major concerns about data quality, noting changes of ~2 counts in 0-6 range may be technical noise and requesting new experiments.

Strong agreement on tetR-KRAB switching mechanism (C22-C24, C78-C83). Both evaluations find this well-supported with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers specifically praise this as 'very nice' and first clear demonstration that histone modifications can turn off CTCF insulation.

Agreement on control experiments (C84-C85). Both evaluations accept that tetR-KRAB effects in del(30-440) background support the mechanism of CTCF displacement allowing enhancer-promoter re-association.
Perfect agreement on temporal dynamics (C25-C26). Both evaluations accept the 16-24 hour timeframe and functional validation through proliferation assays without concerns.

Agreement on differential histone mark kinetics (C27-C30). Both evaluations accept that H3K27me3 follows expression changes with appropriate temporal data, though peer reviewers initially noted delays weren't large enough to exclude alternatives.

Partial disagreement on EPZ experiments (C31-C33, C105). OpenEval finds strong support for challenging threshold model, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, initially questioning whether H3K27me3 levels actually changed and requiring additional ChIP-qPCR data.

Significant disagreement on NEUROG2 experiments (C34-C39). OpenEval finds successful application to second locus with appropriate validation, while peer reviewers raise concerns about 4C data robustness, single population analysis, and possibility of secondary effects.
Agreement on technical aspects of differentiation system (C86-C92). Both evaluations accept transgene silencing explanation and differentiation markers as valid context for NEUROG2 experiments.

Agreement on GSEA/GO enrichment (C60-C61, C99). Both evaluations accept that transcriptome changes link to known MYC functions, though peer reviewers raised concerns about the underlying RNA-seq methodology.

Agreement on background literature (C40-C48). Both evaluations accept these as well-established prior knowledge, though peer reviewers note confusion about how authors discuss mechanisms of loop extrusion vs enhancer blocking.
Agreement on MYC locus context (C49-C53). Both evaluations accept these contextual claims about the MYC locus from literature without challenge.

Partial overlap on extended contacts (C58). OpenEval finds 4C-seq data showing extended contacts well-supported, while peer reviewers question broader chromatin architecture context and request Hi-C/5C data.

Disagreement on mechanistic speculation (C59). OpenEval finds speculation about compensatory contacts reasonable and grounded in data, while peer reviewers question why deletion has smaller effect than STITCH and find explanation inadequate.
Disagreement on directionality analysis (C69). OpenEval finds inference from 4C-seq data well-grounded, while peer reviewers find explanation unclear and part of confusing PCA analysis.
Agreement on NEUROG2 system observations (C86-C87, C92). Both evaluations accept transgene silencing and locus specificity as documented, providing context for interpreting results.
OpenEval identifies C62 as properly cited prior work on mutational analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific background claim.
Perfect agreement on H3K27me3 literature context (C100-C104). Both evaluations accept these citations as appropriate background for interpreting EPZ experiments.
Perfect agreement on PVT1 literature (C106-C108). Both evaluations accept these as accurate representation of prior conflicting findings about PVT1 function.

Agreement on heterochromatin and contacts (C109-C112). Both evaluations accept the finding that heterochromatin doesn't prevent gene-enhancer contacts, though peer reviewers note general confusion about Discussion mechanisms.
Agreement on KRAB context-dependent function (C113-C114). Both evaluations accept that KRAB can have activating effects when targeted to insulators as an important insight.
Agreement on localized effects (C115). Both evaluations acknowledge this as an advantage demonstrated by ChIP-seq showing specificity at MYC without changes at enhancer or control loci.
Agreement on contact domain literature (C116). Both evaluations accept this recent literature citation as appropriate context, though it doesn't directly impact main conclusions.

Partial overlap on generalizability (C94-C98 vs C94, C96). Both evaluations accept cross-species and cross-context validation, with OpenEval providing more comprehensive assessment of system robustness.
Peer reviewers specifically evaluated power law scaling (C14-C15) as highly interesting and important contribution. OpenEval includes these claims in R4 with broader mutational analysis context.
